column1: # The rustc twin's named divergences of programs with no case of their own
# (a translation, a guide block): NAME<TAB>WHY, NAME as the runner prints it
# (tests/translate.sh: SET/NAME; tools/rustc-twin.sh: NAME). A case of
# tests/run says it in itself, `// RUSTC-DIFFERS: WHY` (plan-0271 Q8).

column2: L7: Rust 2021 captures the field (d.id, a copy), not the variable: d is dropped at main's end
L7: Rust 2021 moves only p.a into the closure: p.b is dropped at main's end, p.a with the closure
arrays' by-value IntoIterator (const generics): vole's for x in arr reads the array, dropped at its scope's end; Rust's drops each element after its iteration
vole's bounds failure is one line, FILE:L:C: then 'index out of bounds: index 3, length 3'; rustc's panic message is 'index out of bounds: the len is 3 but the index is 3'
vole's bounds failure is one line, FILE:L:C: then 'index out of bounds: index 4, length 4'; rustc's panic message is 'index out of bounds: the len is 4 but the index is 4'
vole's failed assert is one line, FILE:L:C: then the message and the values of the names in the condition (`k is small: k = 3`); rustc's panic message is the text alone
unordered: the keys of a HashMap in iteration order: vole's is its slot order, the same every run (`ba`); Rust's RandomState gives `ab` or `ba` by run
